newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECT T$4 BLN IN FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECT T$4 BLN IN FUNDS.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, responding to recent tight liquidity in the money market, injected T$4 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operation on Thursday, a bank official said.
The bank executed a repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit, treasury bills and government bonds offered by interested financial institutions with a rate of 7.5 percent, the official said.
The institutions have the option to repurchase the NCDs, treasury bills and bonds within 22 days, he said.
At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate eased to 8.252 percent against Wednesday's 8.601 percent -- still well above the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
On Wednesday, the central bank injected T$27.145 billion worth of funds through open market operation, and in the preceding day, it injected T$35 billion to ease liquidity squeeze.
